minutes.headline: Committee approved an 8th-grade DC trip and heard the town's building plan, urging Turkey Hill not wait.
minutes.summary: The committee approved line-item transfers, a four-day 8th grade Washington DC trip, the FY23 end-of-year report and the strategy action plans. A municipal building design committee representative presented hybrid concepts for the TC Passios, Town Hall and Ritter buildings, prompting debate over debt capacity and Turkey Hill's timeline. The committee also heard MCAS and i-Ready assessment results and scheduled a November workshop on the building plan.

what_happened.line: The committee heard a municipal building design representative present hybrid concepts for the TC Passios, Town Hall and Ritter buildings; no resolution, a workshop was planned.
The committee approved a four-day 8th grade Washington DC trip by a 5-0 vote, with families paying the vendor directly.
The committee accepted a salary and wages line-item transfer on a roll call vote, covering a social worker replacement and moved paraprofessional money.
The committee accepted the FY23 end of year report and authorized signing the submission, then accepted the strategy for continuous improvement action plans.
The superintendent said keeping positions as Esser money ends will force hard budget choices and a request near the usual cap.

why_it_matters: The building concepts and the town's borrowing capacity bear on how much debt the town can take on, which affects future tax bills and the timing of a Turkey Hill replacement.
The superintendent's comment on Esser funding ending points to a school budget request near the levy cap, a figure residents may be asked to vote on at town meeting.
watch_next: School committee workshop on the building plan on November 2, with feedback to the municipal building committee requested by the end of November.
Staffing and five-year forecast discussion scheduled for November 16.
